name: Forced Proximity
summary: Two people who would never choose each other's company are shut into the same space with no exit — a storm, a shared assignment, a locked house, one bed — and the friction of being unable to leave wears the guard down until an involuntary intimacy surfaces that neither planned and neither can now unsee.

roles.label: the point-of-view lead
constraints: cannot leave the shared space

roles.label: the other party
constraints: is the reason leaving matters

roles.label: the circumstance that traps them
constraints: is external and not either party's doing

beats.label: Shut in together
beats.intent: an external circumstance removes the option of leaving

beats.label: Friction under confinement
beats.intent: proximity forces the irritation and the difference into the open

beats.label: The guard slips
beats.intent: an unguarded moment shows the person behind the posture

beats.label: Involuntary intimacy
beats.intent: a closeness neither intended becomes undeniable to both

preconditions.text: two parties with a reason to keep distance from each other

effects.text: the distance between them can no longer be maintained by habit
each has seen something of the other that was not offered

examples.text: The road washes out and the only shelter is one room with one lamp; by the third night the arguing has stopped and neither of them wants to say why.

name: The Misunderstanding That Hardens
summary: One party sees a fragment of something true — an embrace, a letter, a payment — and draws the conclusion the fragment invites. Pride or fear keeps the question unasked, silence sets like cement, and by the time the whole picture arrives the damage is no longer about the misunderstanding at all but about what the silence proved.

roles.label: the one who sees the fragment
constraints: draws a conclusion without asking

roles.label: the one misread
constraints: has an explanation they are not asked for

roles.label: the partial evidence
constraints: is genuinely true and genuinely incomplete

beats.label: The partial truth is seen
beats.intent: a real but incomplete thing is witnessed out of context

beats.label: The wrong conclusion sets
beats.intent: the fragment is completed by fear rather than by asking

beats.label: The silence hardens
beats.intent: pride keeps the question unspoken until distance becomes the new normal

beats.label: The whole picture arrives
beats.intent: the missing context lands, too late to be free

preconditions.text: an attachment strong enough that being wrong about it hurts

effects.text: the attachment between them is left unstated out loud, and unrepaired
trust must now be rebuilt rather than assumed
the habit of not asking is exposed as the real fault

examples.text: She sees the ring pressed into another woman's hand and turns away before the sentence that would have explained it is finished.

name: The Arrangement That Stops Being One
summary: A binding is entered for reasons that have nothing to do with feeling — a debt, an inheritance, a family's face, a visa, a treaty — and the terms are set out plainly so that no one mistakes it for more. The rules are then broken one small clause at a time, until admitting the truth costs more than the arrangement was ever worth.

roles.label: the party who needs the arrangement
constraints: enters for a stated non-romantic reason

roles.label: the contracted partner
constraints: has their own reason for agreeing

roles.label: the family, debt or institution forcing it
constraints: makes refusal costlier than agreement

roles.label: those the arrangement is performed for
constraints: must be convinced it is real

beats.label: The bargain is struck
beats.intent: a binding is agreed for openly transactional reasons

beats.label: The terms are set
beats.intent: explicit rules mark out what this is not allowed to become

beats.label: The rules give way
beats.intent: the terms are broken in small private ways neither party reports

beats.label: The truth costs more than the lie
beats.intent: keeping up the pretence becomes more painful than confessing

preconditions.text: a pressure that makes a loveless binding the rational choice

effects.text: the transactional frame no longer describes what exists
ending the arrangement now has an emotional price neither anticipated

examples.text: Clause four said separate rooms; by winter neither of them could remember which night it had stopped being observed.

name: The Rival Who Forces the Question
summary: A third party makes a claim on someone whose place in the lead's life had never needed naming. The jealousy arrives before the admission does, the comfortable ambiguity becomes untenable, and the lead is made to either stake a claim out loud or watch the question be answered by someone else.

roles.label: the one who never had to say it
constraints: has relied on ambiguity

roles.label: the one being claimed
constraints: is free to choose

roles.label: the rival claimant
constraints: is a genuine option, not a strawman

beats.label: A rival stakes a claim
beats.intent: a third party openly pursues what the lead assumed was settled

beats.label: Jealousy arrives first
beats.intent: the feeling surfaces before the lead has words for it

beats.label: Ambiguity becomes untenable
beats.intent: staying unspoken is now itself an answer

beats.label: Speak or lose the chance
beats.intent: the lead claims it aloud or concedes by silence

preconditions.text: an attachment between them that has been left unstated out loud

effects.text: the relationship's status is now explicit, whichever way it fell
the rival's presence has permanently changed what can be taken for granted

examples.text: He had never once called her anything in particular — until someone else did, at a table full of people, and the word landed like a door closing.

name: The Cost Paid in Silence
summary: Harm falls toward the beloved and the other absorbs it without telling them — a debt settled, a reputation taken, a wound hidden under a sleeve, a name signed away. The concealment is meant as protection but functions as a withholding, so the discovery lands as both devotion and betrayal at once.

roles.label: the one who pays
constraints: conceals the payment

roles.label: the one shielded
constraints: is not told, and would have refused

roles.label: the harm being absorbed
constraints: is real and would have landed

beats.label: The harm falls toward the beloved
beats.intent: a real cost is about to land on the wrong person

beats.label: It is absorbed in silence
beats.intent: the protector takes the cost and hides that they did

beats.label: The concealment breaks
beats.intent: the beloved learns what was paid and when

beats.label: Devotion and betrayal at once
beats.intent: the beloved must hold gratitude and anger in the same hand

preconditions.text: one party is positioned to intercept a harm meant for the other

effects.text: an unrepayable debt now sits between them
the protector's habit of deciding alone is on the table

examples.text: The creditors stopped coming in the spring; it was two years before she learned whose name had replaced hers on the note.

name: The One Who Came Back
summary: An earlier attachment reappears with the unfinished thing still unfinished, and the present relationship is measured against a memory it never agreed to compete with. What is really tested is not who is preferred but whether the old story was ever actually closed or merely left.

roles.label: the one caught between
constraints: never formally ended the earlier thing

roles.label: the present attachment
constraints: is compared without consenting to be

roles.label: the one who came back
constraints: carries the unresolved ending

beats.label: The past walks back in
beats.intent: an earlier attachment reappears without warning

beats.label: Comparison is forced
beats.intent: the present is measured against a memory it cannot answer

beats.label: The unfinished thing is named
beats.intent: what was never actually ended is finally said aloud

beats.label: Close it or reopen it
beats.intent: the past is ended properly or the present is given up

preconditions.text: an earlier attachment that ended without being concluded

effects.text: the earlier story is closed rather than merely dormant
the present attachment knows exactly where it stands

examples.text: Seven years and he still ordered her tea the way she had stopped taking it, and that — not the apology — was what undid the evening.

name: Across the Line
summary: Attachment forms across a boundary the world enforces — rank, clan, wealth, caste, species, faction, the wrong side of a war — and the enforcement is done by people who mean well. The lovers are made to price the crossing in something concrete: an inheritance, a family, a post, a life.

roles.label: the one who would lose least materially
constraints: has the most to gain and the least standing

roles.label: the one bound by position
constraints: their position is real and costly to give up

roles.label: those enforcing the line
constraints: act out of duty or affection, not malice

beats.label: Attachment across the line
beats.intent: a bond forms where the world says it should not

beats.label: The line is enforced
beats.intent: family or institution moves to separate them for their own good

beats.label: The crossing is priced
beats.intent: exactly what must be surrendered is made concrete

beats.label: Pay it or break
beats.intent: the price is paid, refused, or someone pays it for them

preconditions.text: a social boundary with real enforcement behind it

effects.text: one or both have surrendered something that cannot be recovered
the enforcing party's authority over them is settled either way

examples.text: Her father did not forbid it; he simply laid out what marrying down would cost her brothers, and let her do the arithmetic herself.

name: Slow Thaw
summary: A cold or closed party is warmed not by declaration but by accumulation — repeated small mercies that are never remarked on, offered without expectation, until a moment of real pressure reveals how much ground has quietly been given. The arc is the sum of unremarkable kindnesses, and its payoff is retrospective.

roles.label: the one who keeps offering
constraints: offers without demanding acknowledgement

roles.label: the closed party
constraints: refuses on principle, not from dislike

roles.label: the pressure that reveals the change
constraints: forces an unconsidered reaction

beats.label: Refusal as a settled habit
beats.intent: the closed party rebuffs contact as a matter of course

beats.label: Small mercies, unremarked
beats.intent: repeated quiet kindness that asks for nothing back

beats.label: Pressure removes the guard
beats.intent: a crisis forces a reaction before the guard can be raised

beats.label: How much ground was given
beats.intent: both see, retrospectively, how far the thaw had already gone

preconditions.text: a party whose coldness is a defence rather than a verdict

effects.text: the closed party can no longer claim indifference
the change is visible to others who knew them before

examples.text: He had never once thanked her for the tea, and he had never once let it go cold, and that was the whole of it.

name: The Words That Did Not Land
summary: The admission is finally ready and the moment is finally right, and then something arrives that is more urgent than it — a summons, an injury, a departure, a lie already in motion — and the unsaid thing goes back into the pocket. What it costs is measured in what happens next while the words are still unspent.

roles.label: the one about to say it
constraints: has finally decided to speak

roles.label: the one who does not hear it
constraints: would have answered

roles.label: what arrives instead
constraints: is legitimately more urgent in the moment

beats.label: The words are ready
beats.intent: the admission is finally decided on and begun

beats.label: Something more urgent arrives
beats.intent: an event with a real claim cuts the moment off

beats.label: The words go back unsaid
beats.intent: the admission is deferred and the moment does not return

beats.label: What the silence costs
beats.intent: events proceed on the assumption the words were never true

preconditions.text: a feeling that has become ready to be stated

effects.text: the unspoken thing now distorts every decision that follows
the next chance to say it will cost more than this one would have

examples.text: He got as far as her name before the messenger came through the door, and by the time the room emptied she was already on the road.
